newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICA RAND/BONDS CLOSING REPORT.

text.p: South African bonds ruled off Wednesday's official dealings with a smile inspired by U.S. Treasuries which, in turn, were applauding U.S. July retail sales and PPI figures.

"The U.S. figures were good for them and, in the absence of any local factors, good for us. There were a few institutions getting in on the back of the U.S. moves and a couple of offshore guys have been sniffing about," said one bond trader.
At 1405 GMT, the benchmark R150 bond was at 14.03 percent, well below Tuesday's closing rate of 14.105 percent having thumbed its nose at the 14.08 support level.
The U.S. 30-year bellwhether was last yielding 6.632 percent following earlier announcements of as-expected U.S. July retail sales figures and producer price data which indicated no price pressures.

Dealers said the local long bond was unlikely to have the momentum to break below the psychological level of 14.00 percent overnight with Thursday's session expected to be one of consolidation before a possible pre-weekend assault on the level.
"It depends on the money market. It's been held up for a while ahead of the R119 maturity, but it might go better at the end of the week," said another dealer.
The Reserve Bank earlier told Reuters South Africa's money market shortage could decline substantially after the maturity of government's R119 gilt on Friday.
Offered rates for three-month NCDs were steady at between 15.40 to 15.50 percent, while the 90-day BA rate was also unchanged at 14.90 to 14.95 percent.
The South African Reserve Bank said the money market shortage inched lower to 9.589 billion rand on Tuesday after rising to 9.602 billion rand on Monday.
The rand drifted to a stronger close on light turnover as forex players chased carry points and nodded approvingly at the German mark's sustained gains.
The rand was last changing hands at 4.6585/6615 to the dollar from Tuesday's late 4.6650/6680.
"It's been dead boring today. A few guys sold (dollars) around 4.6680 and there was a bit of excitement after the dollar kept under 1.85, but its all on scrappy flows," said one forex dealer.
The dollar/mark dropped following a Bundesbank report which noted a strong appreciation in German consumer prices in recent months.
Dealers said the local unit would hold below 4.66 overnight but was likely to drift back toward 4.67 on Thursday in the absence of market-moving local news.
The rand forward market was torpid throughout the day.
The rand remained mixed against the crosses. It was last quoted 0.3936/3940 against the firmer mark from 0.3992/3996 late Tuesday.
Rand/yen was stronger at 24.7833/8207 from 24.8736/9003. Against sterling, the rand clawed its way into positive territory, finishing at 7.3543/3637 from 7.3637/3731 Tuesday.
Foreigners bought 324.38 million rands worth of South African bonds on Tuesday after selling a net 252.53 million rands worth on Monday, the Bond Exchange said.
Bond Exchange turnover totalled 8.056 billion rand on Tuesday.
